MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 9, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:02 p.m., on May 9, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 4, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Labor Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6(a):
  Agency Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg; Assistant City Manager Keith
  Rattay; City Attorney William Curley; Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz;
  Labor Attorney Peter Brown: Employee Organization: Service Employees’
  International Union (SEIU)

City Council Minutes  1  May 9, 2023
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
at 6:02 pm with all City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley stated the negotiating team updated the City Council but no action was
taken.

INVOCATION: Council Member Ruesch

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim the Week of May 7 through the 13, 2023 To Be Children’s Mental Health
  Awareness Week

  Presented proclamation to Board Member with Extraordinary Lives Foundation (ELF)
  Amy Betonte.

P2. Proclaim "Drowning Prevention Awareness" for the Months of May Through August
  2023

  Presented proclamation to Fire Division Chief / Division 3 Cheyne Maule.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke on Community Choice Energy (CCE) programs. He stated he is now
advocating Orange County Power Authority and asked that the City to reach out to Joe Mosca,
Director of Communications and External Affairs.

Beckett Xu, Rancho Cucamonga: stated his club attended the Multicultural Medley event at the
North Paseo and thanked the City Council for such wonderful event.

William Palma, M.V.: Spoke on an incident in his neighborhood regarding racism. Voiced
concerns that home values will go down. He outlined his two lawsuits he has filed against his
neighbors and a tentative one against the City.

Roger Shao, Lake Forest: Expressed his appreciation on his club’s participation in the cultural
diversity Multicultural Medley at the North Paseo.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Voiced his concerns on the Core Area Vision Plan specifically addressing he
cost, if more bonds will be issued, traffic concerns, and he CC&R’s.

City Council Minutes  2  May 9, 2023
 Tom Moore, M.V.: Supports the progress of the Core Area Vision Plan. He suggested that the City
look into the construction of a pedestrian bridge between Via Angelina and the Montanoso
Recreation Center to serve residents.

Saga Conroy, M.V.: Spoke on the Mission Viejo Town Hall Meeting tomorrow at 6:30 pm at the
Norman P. Murray Center with Supervisor Don Wagner regarding the Opioid Crisis in Orange
County.
Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked various questions regarding Mayor Goodell’s report on (ONOC)
Oceania National Olympic Committees specifically as to economic expectations of residents from
the ONOC, definable and measurable goals and objectives, and what is the strategy to meet these
goals and objectives.
CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 11 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
the Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the regular City Council Minutes for the Meeting of April 25, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated April 14, 2023 in the Amount of $870,115.53

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated April 21, 2023 in the Amount of $3,527,617.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated April 14, 2023 in the Amount of $52,405.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated April 21, 2023 in the Amount of $25,110.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  May 9, 2023
 6.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending March 31, 2023

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending
  March 31, 2023.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2023

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for March 2023

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2023

  Received and filed.

10. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2023

  Received and filed.

12. Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting and Sealing Services

  (1) Approve sixth amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Bonanza Steam
  Cleaning, Inc for the subject services; and (2) authorize a change order to the existing
  Purchase Order for Bonanza Steam Cleaning, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.

13. Annual Routine Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and
  Repairs

  (1) Approved second amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Jamey Clark, Inc
  for the subject services; and (2) authorized a change order to the existing purchase order for
  Jamey Clark, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00.

14. Consultant Services to Produce, Direct and Cablecast Live City Council Meetings for
  Television and the Web

  (1) Approved the first amendment to the existing contract with Eric Winter for the subject
  services for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2025, in the amount of $44,254.98;
  and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2023,

City Council Minutes  4  May 9, 2023
   through June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed $21,556.29 pending adoption of the 2023-
  2025 budget by the City Council.

15. Consultant Services for Coordination of Activities at Mission Viejo Television
  (MVTV)

  (1) Approved the first amendment to the existing contract with Eric Winter for coordination
  of activities at Mission Viejo Television for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30,
  2025, in the amount of $59,565.78; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Eric
  Winter for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024, in the amount of $29,014.22
  pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget by the City Council.

16. Consultant Services for Producer/Director of Various Mission Viejo Television
  Programs

  (1) Approved the first amendment to the existing contract with Eric Winter for the subject
  services for the period of July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2025, in the amount of $174,813.69;
  and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2023,
  through June 30, 2024, in an amount not to exceed $85,150.47 pending adoption of the 2023-
  2025 budget by the City Council.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

11. Amendment to the Management Agreement with AGC Management, LLC for the
  Oso Creek Golf Course

  Council Member Vasquez asked questions and voiced concerns regarding the increase of
  the contract.
  Assistant City Manager explained the reason for the contract increase.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve
  the second amendment to the management agreement with AGC Management, LLC for the
  Oso Creek Golf Course.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Community Services Commission Vacancy

  Motion made by Mayor Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to appoint Saga
  Conroy to the Community Services Commission.

City Council Minutes  5  May 9, 2023
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Goodell.

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Ruesch.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

City Attorney Curley announced that a draft housing element has been submitted to the
Department of Housing and Community Development.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum spoke about the diversity inclusion event the City held at the Civic
Core and that both her and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stopped by the La Paz International Festival
and Market Place which has bee going on for ten years. It showcases all the different heritages at
La Paz Intermediate School. She attended the OCFA Best and Bravest event. Council Member
Bucknum stated she also attended the Marguerite Aquatics Center Water Safety Event that was
very well attended. She encouraged residents to attend the summer event. She attended the
Community of Character 20th Anniversary Event, and gave kudos to Mayor Pro Tem Kelly on all
her work with this committee. She said she had the honor of saying a few words at the National
Day of Prayer that was led by Mission Viejo Christian Church at Florence Joyner Olympiad Park
and was impressed by the turnout. She thanked Commissioner Pam Smith for joining her at the
closing ceremonies of the Mission Viejo Girls Softball League, and stated that the Mission Viejo
Little League ceremonies will be upcoming. Finally, she reminded residents that the Opioid
Fentanyl Crisis event is tomorrow evening at the Norman P. Murray Center and the next Southern
California Sober Living & Recovery Roundtable will meet this Friday in Santa Ana. Lastly, she
announced the bike rodeo and collaboration with the Highway Patrol, also this Friday at the
Marguerite Aquatics Complex and this Saturday is the E-Waste Event at 9:00 am at City Hall, as
well as a Family Arts Day at the Potocki Center. Wished everyone a Happy Mother’s Day.

City Council Minutes  6  May 9, 2023
 Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch attended the OCFA Best and Bravest as well as the OCSD Medal
Ceremony. He attended the Orange County Triathlon. Council Member Ruesch that he attended
the Purse Palooza event. Council Member Ruesch stated he also attended the 20th Anniversary of
Community of Character as well as the Mission Viejo Activities recognition luncheon. Lastly, he
thanked the Mayor for the cool island attire this evening.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated that she also attended the 15th Annual OCFA Best and Bravest
event and commented how challenging it must have been to select the winners. She shared that it
was incredible to see the film and images of the selfless act of these winners. She also attended the
Community of Character Anniversary event and gave kudos to Mayor Pro Tem Kelley. She
announced that she was asked to be on the selection panel for the 2023 Cougar of the Year Award
at Capistrano Valley High School. She mentioned that she will be attending the E-Waste Event
and announced that the Animal Shelter has their Low-Cost Vaccine Clinic this Saturday as well.
Lastly, she said she attended a girl scout even in Carlsbad this past weekend.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley explained that the reason she missed so many events these past six weeks
was because she was in Kansas City where her youngest son received his PhD and he is now Dr.
Mark Kelley. He is a pastor at Compass Bible Church in Aliso Viejo and she is very proud of his
accomplishment. She stated that he was an original member of the Mission Viejo Community of
Character. Prior to leaving town she did attend a Trauma Intervention Program (TIP) awards
event last Thursday April 27. For those that don’t know TIP is an organization of trained
volunteers that respond to traumatic events to assist those in need. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also
announced that she attended the Best and Bravest event. She stated that she was sorry she missed
the Medal of Valor awards and is grateful for both organizations for putting their lives on the line
each day. She thanked the Council, Commissioners, School Board Members and Congresswoman
Young Kim for attending the 20th Anniversary of the Community of Character event. She
announced that the month of May is Moral Courage. She encouraged residents to attend many of
the upcoming events.

Mayor Goodell

21. Report on (ONOC) Oceania National Olympic Committees Brisbane, Australia

  Mayor Goodell presented his report.

City Council Minutes  7  May 9, 2023
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:52 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting in memory of his mother Reba Goodell, to Tuesday, June
13, 2023, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 23, 2023

City Council Minutes  8  May 9, 2023
